input.extraction_context: import ZIP as new slot, later activation
input.reason: a real Java world's region/entity/poi/data files number in the low thousands at most; millions of tiny entries is not a legitimate world shape

expected.check_performed_against: central directory's declared entry count, before iterating entries

notes: D-006 correction, not oracle parity. This is the companion zip-bomb vector to extraction-size-limit-exceeded-rejected: a huge number of near-empty entries can exhaust inodes, memory, or wall-clock time (one filesystem operation per entry) even when total declared bytes stay small, so a size-only limit is insufficient on its own. MSC 1's unzip -o has no entry-count awareness either. Phase 6 checks the declared entry count from the central directory against a fixed ceiling before any per-entry work begins, refusing the whole archive if exceeded -- consistent with every other archive-safety case in this domain refusing at the archive level, not the entry level, once a single entry proves the archive untrustworthy.
